convention: Relationship points are the only number this game settles, and they come from `game-mechanic/closeness-scoring`, whose page holds the rubric. When a scene with a girl ends, spawn a fresh judge subagent handed only that scene's turns and the closeness-scoring page. The judge answers a reading `{ validation, acknowledgment, reassurance, emotionalIntimacy, turnedAway }`, each skill a whole number from 0 to 3 and turnedAway the count of her bids he missed or brushed past, with the words each score rests on quoted verbatim. Settle it with `akasha game settle --game game/the-dating-game --turn <n> --mechanic game-mechanic/closeness-scoring --reading <json>` and no dice: this game rolls nothing, so `akasha story settle` is never its command. Add the answered `change` to `relationshipPoints` on that girl's relationship page. The first time he meets a girl, file her as a character-other at `story/world/pages/personas/stories/played/the-dating-game/characters/the-dating-game-<persona>.character-other.ts`, and her relationship at `story/world/pages/personas/stories/played/the-dating-game/mechanics/relationships/the-dating-game-<persona>.world-relationship.ts` naming `character-player/the-dating-game-alan` and her character, in `world/personas`, at 0 points. Her level is worked out from her points and never written. Every scene with a girl stays inside the closeness-level page her relationship has reached: that rung's stage, wardrobe and pose bound where the two of them are and how intimate the scene gets. Below level 1 she is someone he has only just met, level 5 is intimacy implied rather than shown, and explicit sex waits for level 6. Where he reaches past her rung, she answers as she would at that rung rather than the scene jumping ahead. Score what he did, never how the scene wanted it to go; a run is the game master's to read, never a client payload.
